1.note: The completion of the Temple in Darius's sixth year is at Ezra 6:15. The author's numbering of Ezra (cf. 'Ezra 1, section 4' in seg. 10) may follow a different division; the reference is kept as given.

2.note: Arrian's source was Aristobulus of Cassandreia, not a Jew; the author appears to conflate him with the Jewish Aristobulus. The text is translated as written.

3.note: Dan 11:1 dates the angel's speech to the first year of Darius the Mede, while the vision is introduced in Dan 10:1 as the third year of Cyrus. The author's dating is kept as given.

4.he: והרביעי הנופל ביד אויביו מכל אשר קדמוהו
4.note: The phrase is elliptical. 'Than all who preceded him' seems to echo Dan 11:2 ('far richer than all'), so 'richer' has been supplied in brackets.

5.note: The printed Talmud (b. Kiddushin 72a) reads חלזון (Hulwan); the author's text has חרן, translated here as Haran.

6.he: גנוב הוא את החכם דון יצחק מדעת המעתיק לנוצרים
6.note: The idiom (cf. Gen 31:20) suggests that Abravanel took the idea from the Christian author without acknowledging it. 'The translator for the Christians' probably means Jerome (Vulgate; Commentary on Daniel), but this identification is not certain.

7.note: 'עד כי' is unclear here; it is rendered as 'in truth, as I see it.'
